name: Crucible IronFist Weld-Chem Work Glove
description: Matte charcoal split-cowhide palm reinforced with para-aramid fiber panels across the knuckles and thumb web. The cuff extends four inches past the wrist with a quick-release buckle, accommodating standard chrome forearm flanges. Stitching is double-locked orange thread — visible wear on older pairs shows gray-white fraying at the finger bases. The back panel is perforated nitrile mesh for heat venting.
functionality: Chemical-splash resistant palm, heat-rated to 400°C at brief contact. Quick-release cuff fits over most standard chrome forearm flanges. Knuckle panels absorb moderate impact. Grip-textured palm performs wet or dry.
what_it_says: You work with your hands and you don't expect the job to be safe.
story_hooks: A pair found at a crime scene still has the corrosive chemical residue — the wrong kind for any legal job site in the district.
The worker wearing these has a chrome right hand she's hiding; the glove's flange slot fits perfectly, but she's been telling her supervisor she's fully organic.
Counterfeit versions are flooding the Shelf market — they look identical but the para-aramid is replaced with cheap polyester, and workers are getting burned.
